ai.title: Skip local credit checks, tighten env guard
ai.summary: Credit enforcement bypasses on local env via `env.ENVIRONMENT === 'local'` in `calculateUsage`, returning `limit: Infinity`. `protec` middleware guard tightened from `!== 'production'` to `=== 'local'`, now enforcing checks on staging. `generate-commit-message` action formatting updated. User input logs prefixed with `USER INPUT:`. Changes isolated to `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts` and `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant in a test or pre-release setup (the "staging" environment where new versions are tried out), the system now checks whether you have enough credits before answering, just like it does in the live version. Previously those test setups skipped the credit check entirely, so responses wouldn't count against any limit. If you're running the software on your own computer for development, nothing changes: you still get unlimited credits locally.

ai.title: Backend: implement best-of-3 patch generation
ai.summary: Added `generateBestOfNPatch` to `backend/src/generate-patch.ts` to generate three patch variations in parallel and select the best one via an LLM comparison prompt. This replaces the direct `generatePatchPrompt` call in the main `generatePatch` flow. The comparison prompt evaluates patches on correctness, minimal changes, and readability, explicitly penalizing un-replaced placeholder comments. `applyPatch` from `common/util/patch` is now used to evaluate the generated patches against the original content before comparison.

eli5.text: When the assistant drafts a code change for you, it now writes three different versions first and picks the best one, rather than committing to the first draft. It judges them by how correct they look, how small a change they make, and how readable they are, and it will avoid versions that leave placeholder comments like '//... existing code...' in place. You won't see the pick directly, but the patch applied to your file is the one the system judged to be the cleanest match to what you described. This is live today for the backend flow that generates patches.

ai.title: Support multiple Anthropic API keys
ai.summary: Added ANTHROPIC_API_KEY2 to env schema and updated promptClaudeStream to randomly select between ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY2. This change is scoped to backend/src/claude.ts and backend/src/env.mjs. The selection logic uses Math.random() > 0.5 to distribute requests across available keys.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question, the system now has two different API keys it can use to talk to Anthropic, and it picks one randomly each time before it sends your request. This change is live today and mainly affects the backend, so you won't see a new button or option, but you may notice slightly different behavior if you happen to hit the second key. The new key must match the same format as the existing one, so only authorized setups will recognize it; casual users without that second key won't be impacted.

ai.title: Deterministic API key selection via fingerprint hash
ai.summary: Replaced random 50/50 API key selection with deterministic hashing in `promptClaudeStream`. New `randBoolFromStr` utility in `common/src/util/string.ts` sums character codes of `fingerprintId` to select between `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY2`. This ensures consistent routing per user session, likely to stabilize rate limit handling. Changes affect backend Claude integration and shared string utilities.

eli5.text: Starting today, each person who talks to the assistant is always sent to the same one of two backup pathways, chosen by a fixed tag tied to their account instead of by a coin flip. If you use the assistant across multiple conversations, you will now consistently hit the same pathway every time, which smooths out the chance that your requests get slowed or blocked by rate limits. You won't see a setting or message for this, but your traffic is now routed more predictably.

ai.title: Add ANTHROPICAPIKEY2 to .env.example
ai.summary: Added `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY2` placeholder to `.env.example`. Supports multiple Anthropic keys for load balancing or fallback. No code logic changes in this commit.

eli5.text: The system now has a second backup route for sending requests to its AI helper, so if the main route is busy or stopped working, it can keep going instead of pausing. You would not see this change yourself, but behind the scenes it adds a second spot in the setup notes where a teammate would paste their extra AI key. This is already in place for anyone running the internal tools today.
